design.problem: P24B froze an intake protocol declaring exactly four requiredInputs and a reference consumer an outside team is meant to run from them. Nobody had measured whether that handover is closed. The gap was argued, never measured
design.threeIndependentProbes: one shared isolation helper would let a single bug produce three false verdicts at once, so each probe owns its own copy of its fenced-block reader, closure walk, isolation, spawn and transcript code and imports nothing but node: builtins. The duplication is mandated by the frozen test's own purity assertion, not incidental
design.transcript: one JSON line on stdout, keys dynamic/notCounted/probe/schemaVersion/static/verdict, schemaVersion 1, isolatedRoot redacted, byte-identical on a second run, carrying no repository path and no temp path
design.failClosed: exit 1, empty stdout, exactly one anchored BOUNDARY_PROBE_ERROR:<CODE> line and no verdict anywhere. Codes: INTAKE_BLOCK_UNREADABLE, CLOSURE_UNREADABLE, ENTRY_NOT_DECLARED, CONSTRUCTION_UNMEASURED, CONSUMER_UNREADABLE, GENERATOR_UNREADABLE, HANDOVER_UNREADABLE, PAYLOAD_UNMATERIALIZED
design.exitZeroMeansMeasured: exit 0 means a measurement completed whatever the verdict; INSUFFICIENT and INSUFFICIENT_BRIDGE are successes, not failures. Every verdict is computed from the measurement, never hardcoded: each probe reports SUFFICIENT if the measured facts ever change

probe1.name: declared-input-closure
probe1.static: the transitive non-builtin closure of the four declared inputs is six files; src/application/action-contract.mjs and tools/generate-action-sdk.mjs are declared nowhere in the handover
probe1.dynamic: a fresh tree holding ONLY the declared four runs the handed-over versioned distribution generator and it exits 1 with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND on its own first relative specifier ./generate-action-sdk.mjs
probe1.why: an absent-file list is an argument; a generator that will not load is a measurement, and the verdict rests on the second

probe2.name: contract-construction
probe2.static: the six ActionContract option names are read out of the type itself; 0 of 6 are documented anywhere in the four handed-over files, and the type and its module are named in none of them
probe2.documentedCriterion: an option counts as documented only where the handover names the type that demands it. Bare kind, name and version do occur inside a handed-over generator, as properties it reads off a contract it was already given; that is a consumer of the type and teaches a reading team nothing about what to construct
probe2.dynamic: on the COMPLETE closure, past probe 1's gap, the generator refuses the plain object a doc-following team would build with TypeError renderActionSdk requires an exact ActionContract instance, while the same six values are accepted by the type itself
probe2.why: the refusal is about the missing type, not about the values, and the probe proves that in the same run

probe3.name: payload-materialization
probe3.static: the consumer takes payload-directory and expected-distribution-version; the generator returns an in-memory file map; no handed-over file carries any filesystem write primitive, so materializerInHandover is false and materializerStep is null
probe3.dynamic: materialized OUT OF BAND by the probe the payload is sound (exit 0, status ok, one report line); held the way the handover actually leaves it the consumer exits 1, prints nothing on stdout and emits one DIAGNOSTICS_FAILED line, a code raised at 4 distinct sites in the consumer and therefore naming none of them
probe3.why: a sound payload a team cannot assemble is a missing STEP, not an unsound payload, and the verdict says which. The probe supplying the missing step is recorded as out-of-band and never as the handover supplying it
